sections.changelog:
Fixed

  • **A part number typed on its own now finds its part.** A short code — `bn5p`, `bp4e`, `lj6` — returned a hundred unrelated rows without the product it names anywhere among them. The search did find it, then threw the answer away: a one- or two-row result counts as "almost nothing", which starts the wrong-keyboard-layout rescue, and the rescue keeps whatever result is *larger*. Retyped in the other layout the code becomes a nonsense word that falls apart into a stray letter and a bare digit, and that digit matches half a parts catalogue — a hundred rows beat two, so two correct products lost to a hundred wrong ones. A model the catalogue does not carry is now a requirement for itself rather than for any scrap of itself, so the nonsense variant matches nothing and is never adopted. Measured on a 14 700-product catalogue over every such code in it: 62 codes returned 6103 rows with 8 relevant ones and 56 codes showing nothing they named; the same 62 now return 73 rows, all 73 relevant, none broken. The suggestions dropdown is covered too — there the word under the cursor stays optional, as a half-typed code should, but it is no longer allowed to stand in for itself in pieces. And a query that names a model or a part number and finds something is no longer handed to the rescues at all: rewriting it — into the other keyboard layout, or word by word for typos — returns more rows almost by definition, so six neighbouring codes used to outnumber the one exact answer and bury it under a "showing results for BN52" banner. Measured in dropdown mode over the same 62 codes: the code asked for is now the first row for all 62, and none of them has its query rewritten. Typo correction is untouched for queries made of ordinary words.

Changed

  • **A model modifier is treated as part of the model's name.** "M3" and "M3 Pro", "13" and "13 mini" are different phones whose parts do not interchange, but only the number was protected: the modifier carries no digit, so when the search loosened its demands it dropped exactly the word that decides which phone was meant, and a query for an M3 Pro screen answered with M3 screens. Modifiers following a model number (`pro`, `max`, `plus`, `ultra`, `lite`, `mini`, `neo`, `air`, `fe`, `se`; anything with a digit in it, like `5g`, was already covered) are now demanded alongside it, and a store with its own vocabulary can adjust the list through the `mvweb_ss_model_qualifiers` filter. Measured over 40 model-and-modifier pairs from a 14 700-product catalogue: 344 rows of which 5 lack the modifier, and no query left without an answer. Asking without the modifier is unchanged — it still shows every variant, which is what a shopper who did not specify one is asking for.
  • **A modifier the catalogue never carried returns nothing rather than the neighbouring model.** The last resort of a search that found nothing is to drop the model and answer with whatever matched — sensible for a model nobody stocks, wrong for a modifier: a shopper asking for "M3 Pro" and shown an M3 cannot tell from the listing that the part fits a different phone. That last resort now keeps the modifier, so the query honestly comes up empty and the dropdown offers best-sellers instead.
